blogs.title: Orthogonal Finetuning Explained in Plain Language
blogs.description: Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) is a new way to tweak big image‑generation models by rotating all of their internal neurons at once instead of shifting them randomly with tiny learning rates. Think of each neuron as a point on a high‑dimensional sphere – by applying an orthogonal rotation you keep every pairwise angle between points intact while still changing directions enough to adapt the model for new tasks.

blogs.title: What Is Hyperspherical Energy? The New Tool for Ensuring Quality Diffusion Models
blogs.description: Hyperspherical energy measures how uniformly the neurons on each layer’s unit sphere are spread out. A small difference in this energy before and after fine‑tuning means the model’s internal knowledge remains stable. By constraining the energy to stay constant during adaptation, OFT guarantees that the generated images stay semantically faithful even after being specialized.

blogs.title: Retaining Your Dog in Every Generated Picture: Subject‑Driven Generation with OFT
blogs.description: Subject‑driven generation asks a model to keep the identity of a single subject (e.g., your dog) while changing backgrounds or text prompts. Traditional methods often lose details or swap identities entirely. With OFT’s angle‑preserving updates, you can finetune Stable Diffusion on just a handful of pictures and still see crisp, faithful portraits every time.

blogs.title: From Sketches to Stunning Images – How OFT Enables Powerful Controllable Generation
blogs.description: Control signals such as Canny edges, segmentation maps or facial landmarks guide image creation in ways that ordinary diffusion models struggle with. OFT injects these constraints efficiently by rotating neuron directions so the model follows the input shape faithfully—while measuring success via new control‑consistency metrics like IoU for sketches or landmark errors.

blogs.title: Faster Phenomenon—OFT Trains Quicker and Stabler Than LoRA or ControlNet
blogs.description: Because OFT operates on rotations rather than arbitrary weight changes it explores far fewer directions in parameter space while keeping semantic structures intact. With block‑diagonal orthogonality you can reduce trainable parameters dramatically relative to LoRA’s low‑rank updates—or drop-in adapters such as ControlNet—yet converge two–times faster and maintain robust stability.

blogs.title: Beyond The Paper—What’s Next for Orthogonal Finetuning?
blogs.description: Key challenges remain such as speeding up Cayley transform inversions, exploiting composition of multiple orthogonal matrices across tasks, and removing bias introduced by block subdivisions—all while keeping inference speed unchanged.
